=== FINDING F1 (NOT BLOCKING, NOT THIS PR'S FAULT): proof/39.json DIGEST MISMATCH IS A BASE-BRANCH FAILURE ===
CI on this head shows `lwb-proof-reexecute` reporting:
  FAIL: proof/39.json: python3 scripts/lwb_handoff.py --check: digest mismatch --
    recorded sha256 'ab8f5e3b...', re-run sha256 'ded08fb2...'
I very nearly wrote this up as a defect introduced by this PR, because this PR regenerates HANDOFF.md. I checked before charging it, and it is NOT this PR's:

  on pr/71     : re-run sha256 ded08fb2...  (HANDOFF.md 2975 bytes)
  on origin/main: re-run sha256 4752247...  (HANDOFF.md 2960 bytes)  <- ALSO MISMATCHES
Both differ from the recorded ab8f5e3b..., which was taken when HANDOFF.md was 2961 bytes. The root cause is that proof/39.json records `python3 scripts/lwb_handoff.py --check` with "verifiable": true, while that command's output embeds HANDOFF.md's byte count ("OK: <repo>/HANDOFF.md passes all checks (2961 bytes)"). That output is repo-state-dependent by construction, so the digest breaks for ANY commit that changes HANDOFF.md -- which the handoff protocol requires of essentially every deliverable. It is already broken on main today.

This does not fail CI right now: .github/workflows/ci.yml marks the step "report-only" with continue-on-error: true, which is why main is fully green despite reproducing the same mismatch. I confirmed main's check-runs are 19/19 success.

I also chased the obvious cross-PR consequence -- open PR #62 flips that step to continue-on-error: false -- and I want to record that it does NOT bite, because I expected it to and was wrong: #62 also changes proof/39.json and adds verifiable-detection machinery to lwb_check_proof.py and lwb_record.py, and `lwb_check_proof.py --reexecute` on pr/62 reports "ALL RE-EXECUTED COMMANDS MATCHED". #62 is internally consistent. Recorded as a near-miss rather than a finding.

Each individual statement was true when written; none is true of the branch now. The body is the artefact a human merging this PR reads, and it currently understates the change: a behavioural change to the repo's own merge-gate resolver is not mentioned in it at all. This fails no gate and I am not treating it as blocking, but the body should be updated to name 5517baf before a human merges this.

=== A FALSE ACCUSATION I CAUGHT BEFORE MAKING IT (recorded per the brief) ===
My first pass compared every record's reviewed_commit against the PR's head.sha from the REST API. By that measure all 14 open PRs, every single record, read STALE -- and I was one step from reporting a repo-wide review collapse. That measure is wrong: committing a record advances head past the sha the record names, which is precisely what resolve_reviewable_head exists to correct. Recomputed with the repo's own function, 13 of 14 PRs are properly reviewed and only #71 was not. I am recording this because the brief asks for it, and because the naive check is the one a future reviewer is most likely to repeat.
